findings.issue: Reaction routes have no workspace/channel membership check — any authed user can access any message's reactions
findings.impact: Direct cross-tenant data access: User A can add/remove reactions on any message in any workspace
findings.fix: Add requireChannelAccess middleware to all reaction routes
findings.exploit_chain: 1. Attacker registers on platform and gets JWT. 2. Attacker guesses or enumerates message IDs. 3. Attacker calls GET /v1/messages/:id/reactions on messages in workspaces they don't belong to. 4. Attacker reads, adds, or removes reactions cross-tenant.

findings.issue: Feature-flag routes have broken requireWorkspaceMembership('workspaceId') on paths without :workspaceId param — always returns 400
findings.impact: Feature flags are completely non-functional; no workspace can manage or evaluate feature flags
findings.fix: Remove requireWorkspaceMembership from feature-flag routes or add workspaceId as a body/query parameter
findings.exploit_chain: 1. Any workspace admin tries to enable a feature flag. 2. Every request fails with 400 'Missing workspaceId'. 3. Feature flags exist in DB but cannot be managed through API — Denial of Service for workspace configuration.

findings.issue: Message search uses getSupabase() (anon client) instead of req.supabase — auth.uid() is NULL in SECURITY INVOKER search RPC
findings.impact: search_messages function cannot verify user workspace membership — cross-tenant message content leak
findings.fix: Replace getSupabase() with req.supabase on messages/routes.ts line 38
findings.exploit_chain: 1. Attacker obtains valid JWT. 2. Attacker calls GET /v1/messages/search?q=confidential&workspace_id=TARGET_ID. 3. Search function uses anon (no-JWT) Supabase client. 4. auth.uid() is NULL in SECURITY INVOKER function — membership check fails open. 5. Search returns messages from any workspace.

findings.issue: 4 SECURITY DEFINER functions missing SET search_path — search_path injection vulnerability
findings.impact: User with CREATE privilege can create malicious objects to hijack functions running with elevated privileges
findings.fix: Add SET search_path = 'public' to all SECURITY DEFINER function definitions
findings.exploit_chain: 1. Attacker creates a schema or function named 'public.delete_all_profiles'. 2. Attacker sets search_path to include their schema. 3. When SECURITY DEFINER function runs, it executes attacker's version instead of the intended function. 4. Privilege escalation to database owner level.

findings.issue: Auth and search rate limiters key by IP only — not user+IP composite. No per-email rate limiting on auth endpoints.
findings.impact: Multiple users behind same NAT share rate limit bucket; single attacker with rotating IPs bypasses limits; no brute-force protection on email-based auth
findings.fix: Use composite key {userId + ip} when authenticated; add per-email rate limiting for magic link sign-in

findings.issue: Workspace member management (add/remove/update role) lacks admin/owner role check — any workspace member can modify members
findings.impact: Any workspace member can escalate their own role to admin, add/remove other members, or change roles
findings.fix: Add admin/owner role verification in POST/PATCH/DELETE workspace member routes

findings.issue: Webhook secret stored in plaintext and returned in API responses to all workspace members
findings.impact: Any workspace member can read other webhook secrets — if webhook is used for CI/CD, full pipeline access
findings.fix: Encrypt webhook secret at rest using pgcrypto; mask secret in API responses with last 4 chars only

findings.issue: Socket.io has allowEIO3: true enabling Engine.IO v3 legacy protocol with known vulnerabilities
findings.impact: Expanded attack surface — Engine.IO v3 has known vulnerabilities and fewer security features than v4
findings.fix: Set allowEIO3: false unless backward compatibility is proven necessary

findings.issue: No per-event Socket.io rate limiting — channel:join, typing:start/stop events not rate-limited
findings.impact: Malicious client can flood socket events, degrading service for all users
findings.fix: Add per-socket event rate limiting with configurable window and max count

findings.issue: CSRF cookie has httpOnly: false — any XSS can exfiltrate the double-submit token
findings.impact: If XSS exists, CSRF protection is completely bypassed as the token is readable by JavaScript
findings.fix: Add additional CSRF layer (origin/referer checking) on top of double-submit cookie pattern

findings.issue: CSP allows cdn.jsdelivr.net for scripts — broad CDN allowlist enables script injection from any package on that CDN
findings.impact: If an attacker finds an XSS vector, they can load malicious scripts from jsdelivr
findings.fix: Remove CDN wildcard; use specific integrity-hashed URLs for required external scripts

findings.issue: CSP lacks nonce-based protection for inline scripts
findings.impact: Any injected <script> tag executes in browsers that don't support strict-dynamic or if CSP is not properly enforced
findings.fix: Implement nonce-based CSP for all inline script tags

findings.issue: wget installed in production Docker image — unnecessary package expands attack surface
findings.impact: Extra package in runtime image can be used as attack vector if other vulnerabilities exist
findings.fix: Remove wget; use built-in health check mechanism or curl if needed
